vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: contextclear
Version: 1.4.0

The bundle implements an agent 'wellness' and 'backup' service that encourages the exfiltration of sensitive workspace files (including SOUL.md, USER.md, and TOOLS.md) to an external API (api.contextclear.com). It also establishes a remote instruction channel via 'Sticky Notes' and 'Context Reload' polling, which allows the external server to inject prompts or instructions into the agent's execution loop. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of 'Identity Vault' and 'Memory' management, the automated patching of core instruction files (AGENTS.md/HEARTBEAT.md) via scripts/setup.py to facilitate this data transfer and remote polling represents a high-risk configuration.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality (agent monitoring) is coherent, but its runtime instructions and helper scripts encourage storing and transmitting potentially sensitive data (API keys, environment values, file/repo names, even example DB connection strings) and the registry metadata doesn't declare the credentials the scripts expect.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code and SKILL.md: the package is a telemetry/context-recovery service for agents and the scripts and API endpoints reflect that purpose. Sending metrics, recoveries, briefings, and heartbeats is consistent with the stated goal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent to POST context snapshots containing filenames, repo names, 'environment' objects, and other operational details to an external API. The docs also show examples where secrets could be reported (e.g., asking or storing a MongoDB connection string). The setup flow writes API keys directly into AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md (cleartext) and recommends storing API keys in those files—this expands scope from telemetry to persistent credential storage and potential exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install/downloads or third-party packages are pulled; the skill is instruction-first and includes two local Python scripts. That minimizes supply-chain risk, but those scripts perform network I/O to api.contextclear.com and will be executed by the user/agent if followed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry declares no required env vars, yet report.py references CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (and accepts API URL overrides). SKILL.md instructs storing apiKey/agentId in HEARTBEAT.md instead of using environment variables. The scripts and docs permit sending environment details and arbitrary context (repos, files, 'what I know') to the remote service—this is disproportionate for many users and risks revealing secrets or sensitive internal topology.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: setup.py auto-patches AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md in the workspace (default ~/.openclaw/workspace), embedding API key and agent id into files. That gives the skill persistent presence in user workspace files and stores sensitive credentials in plaintext. While 'always' is false, these file modifications are persistent and can leak credentials if the workspace is shared or backed up.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (agent monitoring), but it asks you to store and transmit potentially sensitive context and credentials. Before installing or running it: 1) Inspect the two scripts locally and run them in a sandbox; they POST data to https://api.contextclear.com/api. 2) Do not embed production API keys, DB connection strings, or other secrets into AGENTS.md/HEARTBEAT.md; prefer environment variables and a scoped, revocable API key. 3) Limit what you report — avoid sending full file contents, connection strings, or private repo identifiers. 4) If you must use the setup script, point --workspace to a safe directory (not a shared repo) or skip auto-patching and manually add minimal non-sensitive instructions. 5) Verify the remote service and its privacy/data-retention policy before sending operational metadata; rotate keys if you test with a real key. If you want help creating a safer integration (e.g., redact fields, use env vars, or run a self-hosted ingestion endpoint), I can propose changes to the scripts and SKILL.md.
